subject: Next steps — tool fanout architecture, auth scoping, and reranker flow for DeepOpt
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Nair <sofia.nair@deepopt.ai>, eng+infra@deepopt.ai
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + proposed patterns for tool fanout, auth, and reranker flow

Thanks again for the demo today — good conversation and a clear signal that DeepOpt will benefit from a lightweight, predictable way to wire external tools into the assistant flow. Below is a concise recap plus three architecture patterns we discussed and the asks we need to kick off a pilot.

What we want to solve in the pilot
- Allow your orchestrator (DeepOpt) to call functions/tools (search, payments, index lookup, policy-check) with safe, observable, and low-latency invocations.
- Provide a clear contract for structured output so downstream services can parse tool responses reliably.
- Support an efficient reranker step (embeddings + neural scoring) to improve result quality without large latency overhead.

Candidate architecture patterns (high-level)
A) Redwood-managed orchestration (Orchestrator-as-a-Service)
  - Redwood runs the control plane: receives user input -> routes tool calls in parallel -> applies reranker -> returns structured combined response.
  - Pros: simpler integration for DeepOpt, Redwood can optimize batching/caching and enforce per-tool quotas.
  - Cons: requires deeper data-plane access (tool credentials or proxies).

B) Customer-driven orchestration (Client-first)
  - DeepOpt keeps orchestration logic. Redwood provides SDK helpers + tool endpoints (tool definitions + validation).
  - Pros: you retain orchestration control and data stays in your flow.
  - Cons: you manage retries, parallelism, and reranker orchestration.

C) Hybrid (recommended to start)
  - Redwood publishes signed tool definitions and SDK helpers for parallel fanout + structured output; DeepOpt orchestrates primary flow but can opt-in to Redwood sidecar orchestration for specific high-throughput routes.
  - Pros: balance of control and operational simplicity; Redwood provides observability and optional fallbacks.

Key design considerations
- Auth scoping: per-tool short-lived tokens (recommended). Do not share long-lived keys across tools. Vault/KMS-backed secrets are preferred in private deployments.
- Structured output contract: JSON envelope for each tool: {tool_name, status, output_type, output, error_code}. We'll provide a small JSON schema for the pilot.
- Reranker flow: retrieve candidates from your vector DB (top-K) -> call Redwood reranker model endpoint (or run an inline reranker) to reorder. We can try both: Redwood-hosted reranker for quality, or an in-customer model to reduce cross-service hops.
- Error handling: circuit breaker + 2 retries (jittered backoff), fallback order: cached result -> degraded response (partial tool set) -> safe failure message and async retry.

Attachments
- integration-diagram-v1.png (simple diagram showing client vs hybrid vs managed routes)
- runbook-tool-defs.md (draft of tool definition schema)

Asks for the pilot (actionable)
1) Confirm preferred pattern: A | B | C (we recommend C to start).
2) Confirm auth path: will DeepOpt provide a vault path for per-tool secrets, or do you want Redwood to hold short-lived tokens in a VPC-secret store?
3) Provide sample payloads for the most common tool calls (search, lookups, create-payment) and a snippet of your vector index content (anonymized).
4) Point to an engineering contact from your side who can join an integration sync (Alex or your infra lead).

Proposed next step: engineering sync week of Apr 26; if agreed, we’ll scope a 2-week pilot with sample traffic and a go/no-go checkpoint.

Thanks — I’ll stand up a pilot spec once we have the answers above.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: Sofia Nair <sofia.nair@deepopt.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 10:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed patterns for tool fanout, auth, and reranker flow

Thanks Karthik — great write-up. A few clarifications from our side: we like the hybrid (C) path and would prefer to retain orchestration inside DeepOpt for now; however, we want Redwood to expose well-defined tool endpoints and an SDK that handles validation, structured output enforcement, and optional parallel fanout helpers.

On auth: we cannot hand over long-lived credentials. We can support a token-exchange flow and will create per-tool service accounts in our Vault. We prefer short-lived (<= 15m) tokens minted by our auth service. If Redwood needs to proxy calls for latency reasons, we can provision scoped tokens with limited permissions.

Reranker: our infra team prefers not to host a heavy reranker model initially. We can fetch top-100 from our vector DB and send to Redwood reranker endpoint for scoring. Latency budget for reranking should be <= 250ms added on top of candidate fetch. Is that realistic?

Alex (eng+infra@deepopt.ai) will be our point for the pilot — looping them into the next thread. We are available week of Apr 26 for the sync; Apr 27-29 mornings PT work best.

Sofia Nair
Head of Product, DeepOpt
sofia.nair@deepopt.ai

> Attachment: runbook-tool-defs.md (we will attach an internal doc with our tool name conventions if useful)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Nair <sofia.nair@deepopt.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed patterns for tool fanout, auth, and reranker flow

Thanks Sofia — sounds good. Quick implementation notes from an integration/ops perspective (so we can scope the pilot accurately):

1) SDK setup (minimal steps)
- npm/pip install redwood-sdk
- redwood configure --env pilot --auth-mode token-exchange --vault-path secret/deepopt/tools
- register tool definitions (a small YAML or JSON file): name, schema, timeout_ms, retry_policy, auth_scope

2) Auth & token exchange
- Support: short-lived bearer tokens minted by DeepOpt (15m), with Redwood validating issuer via JWKS.
- For optional Redwood-side proxy, we support token-exchange (Redwood gets a one-time scoped token from your exchange endpoint).

3) Routing & fanout policy (recommended defaults)
- Default: parallel fanout with concurrency cap N=4 per user request.
- Routing rule: prefer local (same-region) tool endpoint if latency < 80ms, otherwise fallback to proxied endpoint.
- Cost routing: mark certain tools as ‘expensive’ and gate them behind a quality-threshold or user tier.

4) Structured output contract (examples)
- Each tool returns: {"tool_name":"search_api","status":"ok|error|partial","output_type":"list|text|json","output":<opaque>,"error_code":<nullable>}
- Redwood SDK will validate outputs against the tool schema and surface a single combined structured envelope to the orchestrator.

5) Reranker options
- Option A (fast): Redwood reranker endpoint — send top-K vectors and serialized candidates; Redwood returns scored list.
- Option B (local): host a light reranker in DeepOpt; Redwood provides candidate enrichment helpers.
- Both should include a “confidence” field so UI can decide to display or ask for clarification.

6) Error handling policy
- Per-tool circuit breaker (trip if 5xx rate > 10% over 1min).
- Retries: up to 2 attempts with exponential backoff + jitter.
- Fallback order: cached -> partial result -> user-visible fallback + async retry.

7) Observability
- Redwood will emit token-level tracing, per-tool latency histograms, and call-level error tags to the pilot Drive folder.

I’ve attached a short runbook (runbook-tool-defs.md) with schema examples and a suggested set of safe defaults for timeouts and retries. My recommendation: start with the hybrid pattern (DeepOpt orchestrates; Redwood SDK + optional sidecar orchestration for specific user flows). That minimizes surface area for credential handing while allowing us to optimize batching and reranking at Redwood scale if needed.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed patterns for tool fanout, auth, and reranker flow

Per the thread, summary and decisions for the pilot:

Decisions (agreed)
- Pattern: HYBRID — DeepOpt will orchestrate primary flow; Redwood will provide SDK helpers, tool definition validation, and an optional sidecar orchestrator for high-throughput routes.
- Auth: token-exchange with short-lived (<=15m) per-tool tokens. DeepOpt will expose a token mint endpoint (Alex will share details) and Redwood will accept JWKS-validated tokens.
- Reranker: Redwood-hosted reranker endpoint for the pilot (DeepOpt will send top-100 candidates). Target added latency <= 250ms for reranking; we’ll measure and adjust.
- Error handling: default policy (2 retries, jittered backoff, per-tool circuit breaker).

Pilot scope & owners
- Pilot window: Apr 26 -> May 10 (2 weeks of controlled traffic + 1 week of validation).
- DeepOpt PoC: Sofia Nair, Alex (eng+infra@deepopt.ai).
- Redwood PoC: Jordan Blake (integration lead), Marissa Cole (security + KMS). I will coordinate the sync and acceptance criteria.

Immediate next steps (owner / due date)
- DeepOpt: share sample tool payloads + anonymized vector index subset (Alex) — due Apr 16.
- Redwood: circulate pilot spec + test harness + short runbook for token exchange (Karthik) — due Apr 16.
- Schedule engineering sync: proposed Apr 27, 10:00 AM PT (calendar invite to follow).

If that matches your expectations, I’ll send a pilot spec doc and calendar invites. Thanks again — excited to get this moving.

— Karthik
